name: Temporal
title: Qoqi Flow vs Temporal
tagline: Temporal's durability, without the determinism rules.
lede: Temporal replays your workflow from its event history, so your code has to play back identically, forever. Qoqi Flow freezes the state of execution and thaws it at the line it was at. Nothing replays, so nothing has to be deterministic.

cards.title: No determinism rules
cards.text: In Temporal, time.Now, rand, goroutines and ranging over a map are bugs waiting for a replay. A Qoqi flow never runs twice: it is just code.

cards.title: Mistakes caught at compile time
cards.text: A network call outside a step does not compile, and the error shows the path of calls that leads to it. Temporal finds out on replay, in production, or never.

cards.title: One binary, not a cluster
cards.text: No Temporal Service, no Cassandra, no Elasticsearch, no worker fleet. qoqi serve and a SQLite file; PostgreSQL or MySQL to share the work.

code.title: Wait for an answer, or seven days
code.text: The same wait, in Temporal's Go SDK and in Qoqi.

code.title: Plain code, because nothing replays
code.text: Temporal has a replacement for the clock, for sleep, for randomness, for goroutines. Qoqi needs none.

code.title: Shipping a change under running workflows
code.text: Temporal branches on a version marker, kept for as long as old executions live. A Qoqi instance moves to new code at a stage, its state checked against flow.lock.

faq.q: Is Qoqi Flow ready for production?
faq.a: It is at v0.2.0. The language, the runtime and the daemon work end to end, and they are tested by crashing them on purpose after every write. What it does not have yet is years in production. Start with a flow that matters, not the one that holds the company up.
Workflow: impl Flow. Activity: step fn. Signal: an Inbox field. Timer: wait time.after(...). Selector: wait match. Patching: stage, and migrate fn when the state changes shape. Worker: qoqi serve.

faq.q: Do I have to rewrite my services in Qoqi?
faq.a: No. Only the flow is Qoqi. A step that needs your code stays in your service: any server that answers Qoqi's protocol, a signed HTTP POST. qoqi gen writes the typed interfaces for Go, PHP and TypeScript; any other language implements the protocol in a page of code.
Anywhere one binary runs. SQLite on one machine; PostgreSQL or MySQL when several daemons share the work. There is no managed cloud yet.
